(i) the protection provided by bacterial MS channels against osmotic downshift depends strongly on the speed of the osmotic drop and (ii) after an osmotic downshift cells do not lyse in a uniform fashion.
(1) the rate of osmolar change determines the effectiveness of bacterial mechanosensitive (MS channels), and (2) the cell death mechanism of osmotic shock differs from the prevailing paradigm.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mechanosensitive channels in the protection against osmotic downshift.
the role of MS channels in protecting bacterial cells against osmotic stress.
the role of MS channels in the protection against osmotic downshock, and how this role is determined by the rate of osmolarity change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MS channels are not only involved in the protection of bacteria against the osmotic shock, but they are also responsible for the regulation of the osmolarity of the cytoplasm.
the MS channels are effective in protecting the cells from osmotic shock, and the survival rates depend strongly on the rate and the magnitude of osmotic change.
the rate of osmolarity changes is an important factor in the survival of cells exposed to osmotic shock, and that the prevailing paradigm of the mechanism of osmotic shock is incomplete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of osmolarity change, rather than the final osmotic value, determines the survival probability of bacterial cells.
the survival probability of cells depends not only on the final osmolarity, but also the rate of the change.
the survival probability of cells expressing MS channels depends on the rate of change of osmotic downshift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of osmolarity change is a critical parameter in understanding the physiology of MS channel function.
, to fully understand the physiological role of MS channels, one must control the rate at which the osmolarity changes.
